answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 223 answers need 223 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the vertex index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the ridge audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the dune identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator pays for 223 runs and collects one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
